title: DeckTalk per-machine settings file
description: The keys a per-machine settings file may hold, which are the ones that describe this machine rather than the film. A key about the film belongs in the project file, because the file that ships carries whatever the runner believes.

narration.description: These keys govern how the script is turned into audio.

concurrency.description: How many sections `narrate` voices at once.
concurrency.x-hazard: A voice provider limits requests per account, and a busy answer is retried rather than paid twice.

retries.description: How many more times `narrate` asks again when the voice provider answers that it is busy or failed.

cache_dir.description: Directory that holds the take files and their words files, each named by its content hash. It is empty for `build/narrate/` inside the project, and a path here keeps the voiced takes when `build/` is deleted and lets many projects share one cache.
cache_dir.x-range: takes any value of its type

record.description: These keys tune the headless Chromium recording and how narration t=0 is found in it.

browser_path.description: Chromium executable that `record` drives. It is empty for the build DeckTalk fetches itself, and a path here is what a managed machine sets: a named executable that will not launch is never a reason to download another.
browser_path.x-range: takes any value of its type

page_policy.description: How far `record`, `check` and `storyboard` trust a page. `trusted` lets a page reach the network as a browser would. `untrusted` turns the Chromium sandbox on and refuses every request that is not for the project's own origin, through every channel a page can open. It is the machine's to set, so a project someone else wrote cannot trust its own page.
page_policy.x-range: must be one of trusted, untrusted
page_policy.x-hazard: A service that renders pages other people wrote sets `untrusted` on its machine, because a trusted page can reach anything the machine can, including a cloud metadata endpoint.

concurrency.description: How many page sections `record` records at once. Zero chooses from the CPU this process may use, which inside a container is its quota rather than the host's core count.
concurrency.x-hazard: Each recording needs about two dedicated CPUs to present its frames on time, and a starved recording stalls or lands its reveals late, so a number above the machine's share costs correctness rather than only speed.

output.description: These keys switch the files a build writes beside the final mp4 and how long they are kept.

events_max_bytes.description: Bytes one run's events file may reach before debug and info lines are left out of it. Lines about the run, its stages, its sections, its findings and its spending are always kept.
events_max_bytes.x-hazard: A file with no bound grows with every tool call a long film makes, on a disk a host shares.

tools.description: These keys name the tools DeckTalk drives, for a machine that supplies its own.

ffmpeg.description: ffmpeg executable. It is empty for the build DeckTalk fetches itself.
ffmpeg.x-range: takes any value of its type

ffprobe.description: ffprobe executable. It is empty for the build DeckTalk fetches itself.
ffprobe.x-range: takes any value of its type

timeout_seconds.description: Longest one ffmpeg or ffprobe call, or one wait on another fetch of ffmpeg, may run before it is stopped.

cache_dir.description: Directory the fetched Chromium and ffmpeg builds live in. It is empty for the standard per-user cache.
cache_dir.x-range: takes any value of its type

host.description: These keys are facts about this machine that a run measures rather than a person chooses.

presentation_bias_ms.description: How long this machine takes to present a frame the page has already drawn, which is what a run's own measurements of this machine are read against.
presentation_bias_ms.x-hazard: A bias written by hand is a claim about this machine that nobody measured, and the one command that can measure it is beside this key. It is measured or it is zero.
